overall: The three-member Budget Subcommittee violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating over email on a report draft; the AG ordered immediate and future compliance and public release of the quorum emails within 30 days.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged subcommittee members circulated drafts of a budget-process report by email among all three members in Oct. and Nov. 2011.
allegations.key_passage: This series of email exchanges constituted impermissible deliberation.

allegations.summary: Finance Committee argued the email changes were grammatical and not substantive, so they were not deliberation; the AG rejected this.
allegations.key_passage: But the exchange of drafts over the subsequent two months addressed more than mere grammatical edits, such as adding four additional goals for the budget process between drafts.

remedy: We order immediate and future compliance with the law

order the Finance Committee to publicly release all emails from members of the Subcommittee that were sent between and among a quorum of the Subcommittee on matters within its jurisdiction, unless the attorney/client privilege or an exemption to the Public Records Law applies. This should occur within thirty (30) days of receipt of this letter.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law, and order the Finance Committee to publicly release all emails from members of the Subcommittee that were sent between and among a quorum of the Subcommittee on matters within its jurisdiction, unless the attorney/client privilege or an exemption to the Public Records Law applies.
